study: Regeneration-aware GPU multi-seed study on the fixed assumed Bahrain model
primary_endpoint: Final deterministic fine-grid policy from every training seed; no best-checkpoint selection
secondary_endpoint: Final stochastic training/fine/refined paired evaluations with five fixed action-noise seeds; summarize within training seed first
aggregation: Mean, sample standard deviation and range across three training seeds; no significance or convergence claim from this sample alone
conditions: Same 55 decisions/lap, 8 observations, automatic MGU-K recovery, 2 MJ initial/0.1 MJ reserve and 70 m/s start/finish as regeneration pilot; no final-test telemetry
rng_isolation: Every evaluation restores Python, NumPy, torch CPU and all CUDA RNG states; each coarse/fine stochastic member starts from the same evaluation seed
schedule: Constant learning rate and clip range; training state persists across4096-step learn calls; separate evaluation environments
gate: All final deterministic and stochastic replays feasible; training-to-fine gain-versus-zero discrepancy <=0.05 s; additional fine-to-refined paired advantage, lap-time and battery/recovery convergence gates apply to all final pairs
failure_policy: Preserve all failed gates and seeds; aggregate completed seeds without filtering numerical failures. An accepted study requires all three complete and all final replay/refinement gates pass. Do not relax thresholds after observing results.
interpretation: Primary endpoint remains final deterministic 8800-cell lap. The 17600-cell replay diagnoses paired numerical uncertainty. Passing a numerical gate is not evidence of statistical significance; three seeds provide descriptive variation only.
